notes: Canonical construct ids for the 2026-09-30 complete matrix. The answer key (docs/plan/2026-09-30-complete-matrix.md, Part A) and the harness both use these ids; do not rename, only append.
Ids that also exist in tools/interaction-matrix.py keep that name, so old and new counts line up. New ids: keep, op-finditer.
kind: pattern = found in the pattern text; flag = a regex flag (scoped inline or global); op = the operation or its arguments.

family groups ids for the triples. The risky families are call, fuzzy, lookaround, conditional, verb, partial, reverse (7 families, 35 triples). A row is in a family when it has any id of that family.
Pairs are over ids, excluding the pairs in 'impossible'. Every pair and every risky triple needs at least 50 rows.
VERSION0 is the default, so V0 is not an id: a row without flag-V1 is a V0 row.

constructs.meaning: A fuzzy constraint: the item may match with up to n errors of the kinds given (e = any, i = insertion, d = deletion, s = substitution).
A fuzzy constraint with a lower bound: the item must use at least m errors.
A weighted fuzzy constraint: each error kind has a cost and the total cost is capped.
A group call or recursion: run a group's pattern again at this point.
A positive lookahead: succeed if the text ahead matches, without consuming it.
A negative lookahead: succeed if the text ahead does not match.
A positive lookbehind: succeed if the text behind matches (any width in regex).
A negative lookbehind: succeed if the text behind does not match.
An atomic group: once it has matched, its choice points are discarded.
A possessive quantifier: a greedy repeat that never gives back.
A lazy quantifier: repeat as few times as possible first.
A greedy quantifier, including counted repeats.
A backtracking-control verb: (*PRUNE) discards earlier choice points, (*SKIP) also moves the next start, (*FAIL) fails now.
A conditional: take one branch or the other depending on a test.
A capture group, numbered or named; includes the repeated-capture history (captures()).
A branch reset group: each alternative numbers its groups from the same start.
Alternatives, tried left to right.
A backreference: match the text a group captured.
\G: the position where this search started (or where the previous match ended).
\K: leave the text matched so far out of the reported match.
Line and string anchors.
Word boundaries.
A character set, including V1 set operations.
A named list: \L<name> matches any string in a list passed as a keyword argument.
BESTMATCH: return the fuzzy match with the fewest errors instead of the first one found.
ENHANCEMATCH: improve the first fuzzy match found by trying to reduce its errors.
REVERSE: search backwards, from the end of the text.
IGNORECASE (simple case folding in V0).
FULLCASE: full case folding (with i), so one character may match two.
VERSION1 behaviour (set operations, zero-width splitting, full case folding by default with i).
WORD: Unicode default word boundaries and line breaks.
POSIX: leftmost-longest match instead of leftmost-first.
search: the first match anywhere.
match: a match that starts at the start position.
fullmatch: a match that spans the whole text (or slice).
finditer: every non-overlapping match, in order (stands for findall, sub and split too).
partial=True: also report a match cut off by the end of the text, when some continuation could complete it.
pos and endpos arguments: search only inside a slice of the text.

impossible.reason: regex raises 'BESTMATCH and ENHANCEMATCH are mutually exclusive'
